dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Corticobasal degeneration (corticobasal syndrome), likely a 4R-tauopathy presenting as a sporadic neurodegenerative disorder.

Alternatives to consider:
1. Multiple System Atrophy (parkinsonian type) — asymmetric parkinsonism with dystonia in a young patient, though typically with autonomic failure and pontocerebellar/basal ganglia MRI changes
2. Young-onset (dopa-responsive) dystonia-parkinsonism — e.g., PARK2/PINK1-related, though resting tremor and alien-limb features would be atypical
3. Huntington's disease (Westphal variant) — can present with rigidity and dystonia in young adults without obvious chorea, though family history is absent and caudate atrophy on MRI was not reported
